test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath

writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.

separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The probes inspect the item embedding table (`item_emb.weight`) and sequence features returned by `log2feats(sequence)`. Model implementation is not supplied, so the internal encoder and final user representation cannot be identified. Margin diagnosis uses features at every valid sequence position, rather than explicitly selecting the final user state.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` accesses the compatibility view’s embeddings, `log2feats`, `predict_score`, and metadata. The supplied constructor names this argument `model`; under the adapter contract, the actual trained module is `view.model`.

Training batches contain `(None, sequence, positive, negative)`, each tensor shaped B × L. The probe computes sequence features, stacks positive and negative IDs into B × L × 2 candidates, and calls `predict_score`. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded. `user_train` and `review_data` are stored but unused.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding collapse:** Excludes padding and samples up to 2,048 item embeddings with seed 42. After normalization, mean off-diagonal cosine similarity is mapped to [0,1]. Higher values indicate stronger directional alignment; approximately 0.5 corresponds to zero mean cosine similarity. This is a geometric proxy, not recommendation diversity.
- **Positive–negative margins:** Over at most ten training batches, computes positive score minus negative score. Higher mean and 10th-percentile margins suggest stronger separation. Lower negative-beats-positive and small-margin rates are preferable; the latter uses threshold 0.5.
- **Category breakdown:** Counts category occurrences for positive and negative items in low-margin and wrong-ranking cases, retaining the top twenty categories. Categories are unavailable in this benchmark, so these lists should remain empty.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, ablation, or input perturbation occurs. Random embedding subsampling and supplied training negatives are the only sampling mechanisms. Margin computation runs in evaluation mode without gradients.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`, containing the six named metrics above and their descriptions. The interpreter prompt separately requests a JSON interpretation with status, findings, implications, and evidence.

These probes assess sampled embedding geometry and training-pair separation. They do not measure validation HR@10, generalization, full-catalog recommendation quality, behavioral traits, or sequence-order sensitivity. Margins depend on score scale and negative sampling. Empty valid-position samples produce zeros, which must not be mistaken for healthy performance.

History perturbations offer useful diagnostics, but ranking changes alone do not establish current intent. [Does It Look Sequential? (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008) compares original and shuffled histories across 15 datasets, finding weak sequential structure in several popular benchmarks. [Disentangling User and Item Sequence Patterns (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748042) shows that ordinary shuffling confounds user behavior with item availability; constrained shuffling respects items’ first appearance. [Measuring Recency Bias (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) proposes measuring excessive dependence on recent interactions. [Higher-Order Sequence Modelling (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19833) finds that simple recency-weighted pairwise models can outperform Transformer reproductions on several benchmarks, suggesting that useful history dependence need not imply complex sequential reasoning.

Practical synthesis: freeze the trained model and compare removal of recent interactions, older history, and repeated-item occurrences against repeated random deletions of equal size. Where feasible, match controls on item popularity, repetition frequency, and history position; vary one factor at a time. Test order separately by shuffling while preserving the item multiset, optionally holding the latest item fixed. Keep candidate sets, padding conventions, and seen-item exclusions identical across conditions. Report paired validation HR@10 changes alongside top-10 overlap and rank displacement; bootstrap users within each category, then macro-average category effects. These controls and intervals are proposed diagnostic design choices, not a verified common protocol from the cited papers. Interpret excess sensitivity over controls as model dependence on particular history evidence. Repeated preferences require observed repetitions or explicitly defined title/description similarity; neither sensitivity nor semantic similarity proves user intent.

train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The probes inspect the item embedding table (`item_emb.weight`) and sequence features returned by `log2feats(sequence)`. Model implementation is not supplied, so the internal encoder and final user representation cannot be identified. Margin diagnosis uses features at every valid sequence position, rather than explicitly selecting the final user state.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` accesses the compatibility view’s embeddings, `log2feats`, `predict_score`, and metadata. The supplied constructor names this argument `model`; under the adapter contract, the actual trained module is `view.model`.

Training batches contain `(None, sequence, positive, negative)`, each tensor shaped B × L. The probe computes sequence features, stacks positive and negative IDs into B × L × 2 candidates, and calls `predict_score`. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded. `user_train` and `review_data` are stored but unused.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding collapse:** Excludes padding and samples up to 2,048 item embeddings with seed 42. After normalization, mean off-diagonal cosine similarity is mapped to [0,1]. Higher values indicate stronger directional alignment; approximately 0.5 corresponds to zero mean cosine similarity. This is a geometric proxy, not recommendation diversity.
- **Positive–negative margins:** Over at most ten training batches, computes positive score minus negative score. Higher mean and 10th-percentile margins suggest stronger separation. Lower negative-beats-positive and small-margin rates are preferable; the latter uses threshold 0.5.
- **Category breakdown:** Counts category occurrences for positive and negative items in low-margin and wrong-ranking cases, retaining the top twenty categories. Categories are unavailable in this benchmark, so these lists should remain empty.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, ablation, or input perturbation occurs. Random embedding subsampling and supplied training negatives are the only sampling mechanisms. Margin computation runs in evaluation mode without gradients.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`, containing the six named metrics above and their descriptions. The interpreter prompt separately requests a JSON interpretation with status, findings, implications, and evidence.

These probes assess sampled embedding geometry and training-pair separation. They do not measure validation HR@10, generalization, full-catalog recommendation quality, behavioral traits, or sequence-order sensitivity. Margins depend on score scale and negative sampling. Empty valid-position samples produce zeros, which must not be mistaken for healthy performance.
